::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
A small, export-led packaging unit in the ELCINA electronics cluster at Bhiwadi, Rajasthan's first semiconductor plant. PIB calls it the first SME to start commercial production of semiconductor chips in India. It was set up with support under MeitY's SPECS component scheme, not the India Semiconductor Mission.
:::

## What does this facility make?

Packages memory chips for microSD cards and flash storage, plus LED driver ICs, eSIMs and RFID products, in a 57,000 sq ft unit with Class 10K and 100K cleanrooms. Capacity is 60 million units a year, with plans for 400-600 million in two to three years. The company says it is starting its own product R&D, including LED driver chips.

## Why does it matter?

Over 60% of output is exported (US, Germany, France, Eastern Europe, China, Nepal), so this is working commercial OSAT capacity today, unlike several larger announced projects. It is low-complexity packaging, but it shows that mid-sized firms can enter the industry through smaller schemes like SPECS and state policy (Rajasthan's Semiconductor Policy, March 2026).
